label: header
text: TUESDAY, MARCH 16, 1926.

label: paragraph_title
text: VERY PROSPEROUS

label: text
text: The school year has been a very prosperous and encouraging one. We closed earlier than usual for the summer vacation, with a full school. We re-opened in September with almost our usual numbers. Boarders, from far distances, such as Formosa, Peking, and Tientsin were unable to return. I am glad to have this opportunity of expressing my grateful appreciation of the loyal manner in which the girls and Chinese staff supported us through troubleous days. Each one seemed to realise the worth of the words used by H.E. the Governor, soon after his arrival in Hongkong.

label: text
text:
this afternoon's annual prize-giving at St. Stephen's Girls' College, the Principal (Miss E. Middleton Smith) said:—
Lady Clementi, my Lord Bishop, ladies and gentlemen,—It affords me great pleasure to welcome you here this afternoon. It is especially pleasing to have with us, Lady Clementi, who has graciously contented to act on our college council in the place of Lady Stubbs. We gratefully remember the sympathetic and keen interest which Lady Stubbs always took in our school activities and although now absent she continues to do so. We are confident that we shall receive from Lady Clementi that kindly sympathy and generous understanding which will indeed be a help and encouragement in our school life. We thank her for kindly coming to present the scholarship, cups, and certificates to-day.

label: text
text: “Education is a process which aims at drawing out, from every human being the utmost which he or she is capable of giving in the cause of ‘humanity.’” I would lay stress upon this word ‘humanity’ and remind you of a famous phrase in the Chinese classics “Within” the flourish “seas all are brothers.” We realise the truth of this saying in St. Stephen’s.

label: paragraph_title
text: Excellent Report.

label: text
text: I will not hire you with a detailed report of the school work. Sufficient is it to say that the standard this year, and this despite anabnormally long vacation—has been higher than at any previous time. We had an excellent report, after the visit of the Government inspector, who specially commented favourably upon history, reading and recitation in the upper school. (Elocution is well taught by Miss Hazeland.) The script writing in the lower school was mentioned as being very good, when the K.G. received special mention, as being well taught and well equipped. (This is in charge of Mrs. Cooper.)

label: text
text:
Dr. Minett visited the school in November last and to quote her own words she found the general health and development excellent. Continuing, she said: "I heard good singing lessons being given for chest and throat development in the upper school." For the singing well taught we are indebted to Mr. Mason. "I saw excellent work being done in drilling and breathing exercises and ball games in the playground under Miss Shi (our physical culture mistress). The K.G. Classes were having good singing and games given in an interesting way. Hygiene is very well and practically taught, the text books in use are the most modern I have seen."
Eight students were presented for the University matriculation and senior examinations. Of these six passed, two matriculating and four passing senior two

label: paragraph_title
text: Englishwoman's Gift.

label: text
text: Nine took the junior examination. Of these seven passed, six gaining distinctions. The two who matriculated have already entered the University in the Faculty of Arts. Another old S.S.G.C. student has entered the University this term. She has been given a scholarship through the generosity of an Englishwoman, who wishes to remain unknown. The gift was a token of friendship to the women of China, the desire being to help a Chinese girl to gain knowledge in the University, in order to give that knowledge to her own people, in a part of China where education is less advanced. We are grateful to the Vice-Chancellor for kindly suggesting that a S.S.G.C. student should accept it.

label: text
text: Most of our girls go into residence at the women's hostel. May I here stress the value of residence in Hall? We are convinced that our hostel life is binding together Chinese students from different parts of China and there are few things for which we should be more grateful to a generous benefactor than a permanent hostel. The women under

label: text
text: graduates are at present in St Stephen's Hall which is a rented building and far too small for the important work. Miss Vincent, B.A., the acting Warden, with wise guidance seeks to help them in every way. Before proceeding with the work of the school, may I mention an excellent scheme which our Society has put into action this year? S.S.G.C. and "Fairlen" together now form a combined institution, S.S.G.C. giving an English and Chinese education, "Fairlen" giving a purely vernacular education: Mrs. Cheung is a very capable Headmistress, while Miss Atkins is giving splendid help as adviser and Warden. Through the generosity of Chinese gentlemen, who have given scholarships; it is possible for a girl to pass from the vernacular school, through S.S.G.C. to the University in this combined scheme of education. There are almost five hundred students in the three institutions, each having its own "Head," with a Principal over all. Very few schools possess staffs who have higher qualifications than those possessed by the staff of these schools. I wish here to pay an unqualified tribute to the whole-hearted devotion of the entire staff to the interest of both schools and their excellent teaching work. The work has been curtailed for lack of room and the need of the extension wing is very great indeed.

label: text
text:
Gifts for Charity.
This year the girls have made a special effort to help the pressing claims of those in need. Over $8,000 has been given to different charities during the year, and we have felt it a privilege to help poor schools and hospitals in different parts of China as well as a contribution of $1,300 to the M.C.L. funds this year. The missionary spirit has been fostered and has grown in the school. Sunday by Sunday our girls teach the unfortunate women in prison. Other girls from this school may be found in the hospital each Sunday going from bed to bed, carrying words of cheer and comfort as they tell of God's love and care for the sick and suffering.

label: text
text: A large number of poor children from Wanchai were entertained at Christmas in our playground and a party of girls visited the hospital and sang carols to the patients at Christmas time.

label: text
text: This spend of helpfulness is shown even after the girls leave school. Life behind them. When in the Philippine Islands last year, I found that one of our old girls, while attending lectures at the University was devoting her afternoons to teaching in a school for poor Chinese children. Classes to give amahs and muitsnis free education are taken regularly on Tuesday and Friday afternoons. Nancy Ho, a past student kindly gives a loving hand each week to help in this work.

label: text
text: "Old" Girls' Association.

label: text
text: The boarders owe much to the thought and care of Miss Wise, B.A., while the lower school and afternoon Chinese studies owe much to the careful teaching of our Chinese staff, too large to mention individually. The standard of Chinese studies has improved under the care of Mr. L. Kwan-shing, our director of Chinese studies.

label: text
text:
A delightful request came from old S.S.C. girls for the establishing of an association to link them together. This was formed with a large membership a short time ago, Miss S. A. Wan being elected as President. This association, we feel, will revive, and help to keep keen, the interests of girls in all parts of the world who have had their education in this school.
Seven girls were confirmed last year and three baptised. Weekly Bible study classes have been much appreciated. A baptism class held by Mr. Li Di-ku, has been well attended. Many other activities have been organised by our school, Y.W.C.A., with the splendid help of Miss Pope, B.Sc., our energetic faculty adviser.

label: text
text: Keener interest in games has been shown and one of our pressing needs is another tennis court. W. only possess one, for the use of the school and S.S. Hall. Some of the girls remember a delightful visit to H.M.S. "Hermes," which Mr. Powell kindly made possible. Others spent a happy afternoon on the "Tamar" where Mrs. Stirling very kindly entertained them.

label: text
text:
Before asking Lady Clementi to present the scholarship cups and prizes may I explain that the successful students receive the cups and certificate only; they generously give the money to educate a girl unable to pay the school fees. We choose girls, who, after completing their education here will teach in other schools in China. The books to be given are a small appreciation of the voluntary work done by two girls. label: paragraph_title
text: THEFTS

label: text
text: The theft of a portable phonograph and records (total value $350) from the Brunswick Studio at Ice House Street has been reported to the police by Miss Olga Carvalho.

label: text
text: The machine was apparently there when the establishment closed on Thursday evening, but was found to be missing the following morning. An examination of the drawers holding records showed several to be also missing: No clue has been obtained as to how the articles were removed.

label: text
text: A Chinese amah working at No! 89, Cuine Road, reported that she lost a bag containing her clothins, money and jewellery (total value $107.50) from her, cubicle yesterday.

label: text
text: A Chinese boy was bitten yesterday by a dog belonging to a widow living at Shelley Street. The animal was taken to Kennedy Town for observation.

label: text
text: The sage Mencius once said: "A really great man or woman is one who, in the fulfilment of duty, will be above the power of riches and honour to tempt, of mean condition to make swerve from principal and of threats and force to make bend." Where are such women coming from? It is our hope that such women are coming from the Christian schools of China and so in the words of our school motto "In Faith we go forward."

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: Evidence relating to the recognised custom of shippers and agents was given in the Summary Court this morning when the case came up for discussion again of the plaintiffs A. P. Moller (claimants for return of commission on collected freights taken by Thóressem and Co., their accredited agents).

label: text
text: Mr. M. H. Turner was for Thoresen's and Mr. T. G. Bennett for A. P. Moller.

label: text
text: Mr. Yates, a local shipping agent, who was called by Mr. Turner with reference to the question of usage said, when questioned by His Lordship, that ship owners and holders of agencies in making a contract of this description understood that there was a duty of the agent of collecting freight but that that duty carried with it an addition to the agents' fees.

label: text
text: witness said that it freight was chargeable and there was an agent in the port where a ship was to discharge it was the ordinary duty of the agent to collect the freight. If an owner appointed an agent, it was the duty of the agent to do everything which the owner would do if he

label: text
text:
Mr. Bennett: Suppose there had been nothing in the contract between these two parties about remuneration and if had just read: "Offer" you agency, Sally Macrsh's Swatow, Amoy. (omitting the reference to $150) would you have considered that authority to collect freight if freight was collectable in Swatow and Amoy?
Mr. Yates: Yes.
Mr. Bennett: You are limiting the meaning of the word "agency" to mean entrance and

label: text
text: Mr. Bennett suggested that the limitation witness was placing on the meaning of the word agency was caused by the inclusion in the contract of the sum of $150.

label: text
text: Mr. Yates, Or of any other sum.

label: text
text: Mr. Bennett: "Supposing no remuneration at all was mentioned would you still have implied the words 'entrance' and clearance only."

label: text
text: "Mr. Yates: In that case the agent would carry out his ordinary duties and charge the customary fees."

label: text
text: Mr. W. G. Goggin also was called by Mr. Turner and supported the evidence given by Mr. Yates. The case is proceeding.

A chair in which King William II had a both pulled, has been presented to Comber, County Down, Orangemen, by John Miller Andrews, a member of Sir J. Craig's cabinet. The fortunes of the chair can be traced without a break for 235 years. Like all relics connected with the king who conquered his royal father-in-law, James II. in the battle of River Boyne, in 1690, it is looked upon with reverence in Ulster.
NAVAL BASE AND RUBBER ESTATES

label: text
text: QUESTION IN COMMONS:

label: paragraph_title
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text:
In the House of Commons, in reply to questions, Mr. L. S. M. Amory, Secretary of State for the Colonies, said that he had received representations to the effect that the demands for labour for the Naval Base at Singapore were depleting the supply of the rubber plantations, but the Governor (Sir. Laurence Guillemard) has assured him that the total requirements of the Naval Base were not sufficient to have any marked effect on the labour situation in Malaya.
The Government of Malaya was closely watching the situation with the local representative of the Admiralty.

label: text
text: Commenting on a previous reference to the same question in the House of Commons the Strals Echo (Penang) said: After denying with oaths that they were paying more than standard rates of wages to the collies employed on the Base works in Singapore, the Naval authorities have now been obliged to admit, through their official spokesman in the House of Commons, that "the wages of Admiralty employees exceed those on plantations." Labour the Base, of course, must have, but it ought not to be allowed to crimp other people's or disorganise the whole situation by paying ridiculous rates. The fair and proper thing would be for the Admiralty to arrange through the Labour Department to import its own coolies from China and India and to pay them the wages generally ruling for the class of work they are called upon to perform.

label: text
text: Cleveland (Ohio), March 15. Millionaires, manufacturers, real estate men, also Government employees in twelve cities are involved in a 40,000 word indictment, naming 112 persons alleged to be concerned in a boot-legging, conspiracy, returned by the Federal

label: text
text: The indictment alleges that the conspiracy originated from four Philadelphia boot-leggers, who made their headquarters in Cleveland and created an organisation for the concentration and distribution of a contraband supply of pure-grain alcohol.

label: text
text: The operations, it is alleged cover a period of three years.
